Score Life's Essential 8 cardiovascular health

Source: R/score-le8.R
score_le8.Rd

Computes the eight adult Life's Essential 8 (LE8) component scores and the composite score using the American Heart Association's 2022 Presidential Advisory. Component scores are calculated wherever sufficient inputs are available, without imputing missing values. This implementation applies only to adults aged 20 years or older.

Usage

score_le8(
  data,
  diet_method = "mepa",
  mepa_columns = NULL,
  min_components = 7L,
  dash_columns = NULL,
  dash_cutpoints = NULL,
  hei2015_columns = NULL,
  hei2015_cutpoints = NULL,
  reference = "nhanes_2015_2018"
)

Arguments

data

A data frame with one row per adult and the input columns described below.

diet_method

A single diet-scoring method applied to every row in data: "mepa" (the default), "dash", "hei2015", or "percentile". Values are matched case-insensitively. Score data that use different methods in separate calls.

mepa_columns

NULL, or a named character vector mapping canonical MEPA fields to columns in data. The names are canonical fields and the values are actual column names. Unmapped fields use their canonical names.

min_components

A single integer from 1 to 8 specifying the minimum number of non-missing LE8 component scores required to calculate le8_composite_score. The default is 7. Available component scores are averaged without imputation; observations below the threshold receive NA_real_.

dash_columns, hei2015_columns

NULL, or named character vectors mapping canonical DASH or HEI-2015 fields to columns in data. Unmapped fields default to the canonical name prefixed with dash_ or hei2015_. Names and input column names are matched case-insensitively.

dash_cutpoints

NULL to use the packaged DASH intake quintiles and total-score cutpoints, or a named list containing the eight canonical DASH fields and total. Each intake vector contains four nondecreasing reference quintile cutpoints (20th, 40th, 60th, 80th percentiles), in the same units as the inputs. total contains four nondecreasing reference DASH-total cutpoints (25th, 50th, 75th, 95th percentiles), each from 8 to 40. Tied cutpoints are allowed. Explicit cutpoints bypass reference and use inputs in their supplied units, without energy standardization, preserving existing calls.

hei2015_cutpoints

NULL to use reference, or four nondecreasing reference HEI-2015-total cutpoints (25th, 50th, 75th, 95th percentiles), each from 0 to 100. Tied cutpoints are allowed.

reference

"nhanes_2015_2018" (the default), or a method-matched diet_reference() object. Used for already-computed indices and raw intake scoring when explicit cutpoints are absent. Raw DASH requires the packaged reference's intake quintiles; for other DASH definitions, supply dash_cutpoints. Direct percentiles and explicit raw cutpoints bypass reference lookup. The built-in references describe nonpregnant adults aged 20+ with two reliable recalls; they are derived estimates, not AHA-published cutpoints.

Value

A data frame containing the original columns plus mepa_total, dash_total, and hei2015_total (missing unless calculated from the corresponding raw inputs), physical_activity_moderate_equivalent_minutes, the eight component score columns prefixed with le8_, le8_n_components, le8_composite_score, le8_complete, and le8_category. The component count reports how many scores contributed to the composite score; le8_complete is TRUE only when all eight components are available. Categories are "low" for scores below 50, "moderate" for scores from 50 to less than 80, and "high" for scores of at least 80. The category is missing when the composite score is missing. For raw HEI-2015 calls, the 13 component scores are also appended as hei2015_<component>_score, including fatty_acids and saturated_fats.

Diet scoring methods

MEPA retains the individual assessment pathway. For population research, diet_method = "dash" accepts an already-computed index in dash, and diet_method = "hei2015" accepts an already-computed index in hei2015. Either method alternatively accepts a percentile in diet_value (0 to 100). Both methods also calculate raw totals from the intake fields below, using the packaged reference by default. Raw HEI-2015 also accepts a custom diet_reference(); raw DASH supports custom definitions via dash_cutpoints. Do not supply both the index column and the percentile column. Data with no diet inputs retain the package's usual missing-component behavior.

An index is compared with fixed reference cutpoints to identify its percentile category. The package does not estimate an exact percentile from four cutpoints, or rank the current cohort against itself. Specify reference = "nhanes_2015_2018" explicitly in reproducible analyses.

The built-in DASH reference is specifically the 8-to-40 Fung-style FPED construction identified as essential8_fung_fped_v1; it requires matching food definitions, pooled weighted intake quintiles, and tie handling. Other DASH definitions need a custom reference. HEI-2015 indices must be constructed using an appropriate established method; the built-in reference uses individual scoring after averaging the same two recalls' constituents and energy. It is not a usual-intake or population-ratio estimate. Both references use NHANES 2015-2016 and 2017-2018, two-day dietary weights divided by two, and the NHANES strata and PSU design. Detailed methodology, source URLs, hashes, sample counts, and index definitions accompany the references and the maintainer script data-raw/build_diet_references.R in the repository.

Fractional inputs confined to 0-1 (other than endpoints alone) are rejected as apparent proportions; supply percentile points, such as 95, not 0.95. This safeguard also rejects a batch consisting only of genuine fractional percentiles below 1. Values are never automatically multiplied by 100.

Supply one input pathway per call: raw intake, a precomputed index, or a percentile. Raw intake fields cannot be combined with a precomputed index or observed percentile. Raw fields are food-group and nutrient summaries, prepared before scoring; the function does not parse dietary-recall files. See vignette("population-diets") for executable examples and units.

Input columns

  • age: Age in years; must be present, complete, and at least 20.

  • For diet_method = "mepa", the 16 Table C screener-item columns named below and sex (or female when sex is absent). The item names are matched exactly after case normalization. Supply daily servings in olive_oil, green_leafy_vegetables, other_vegetables, and whole_grains; supply weekly servings or frequency in berries, other_fruit, meat, fish, chicken, cheese, butter_cream, beans, sweets_and_pastries, nuts, and alcohol; supply the number of times per week that fast-food meals are consumed in fast_food. Sex may be encoded as "m"/"f", "male"/"female", or 0/1, where 0 is male and 1 is female. Character encodings are matched case-insensitively, and character "0"/"1" values are also accepted.

  • dash or hei2015: An already-computed index for the selected population diet method. HEI-2015 is bounded by 0 to 100. The built-in DASH reference requires its documented 8-to-40 definition; custom DASH references can specify other index ranges. These columns are unrelated to MEPA.

  • For raw DASH scoring, supply daily intakes in dash_fruits, dash_vegetables, dash_nuts_and_legumes, dash_whole_grains, dash_low_fat_dairy, dash_red_and_processed_meat, and dash_sweetened_beverages; supply sodium in mg/day in dash_sodium. Canonical mapping fields omit the dash_ prefix. Fruits include juice; vegetables exclude potatoes and legumes. Food groups and serving definitions must match the reference. With the packaged reference, also supply positive kcal/day in dash_energy_kcal; sodium is standardized to 2,000 kcal before scoring. Other fields must use the FPED-derived units and definitions in vignette("population-diets"), including fruit cup equivalents, whole-grain ounce equivalents, and the specified vegetable, dairy, protein, and beverage conversions. With explicit dash_cutpoints, energy is not required and no standardization is applied.

  • For raw HEI-2015 scoring, supply hei2015_energy_kcal (positive kcal/day, including alcohol); cup equivalents/day in hei2015_total_fruits, hei2015_whole_fruits, hei2015_total_vegetables, hei2015_greens_and_beans, and hei2015_dairy; ounce equivalents/day in hei2015_whole_grains, hei2015_total_protein_foods, hei2015_seafood_and_plant_proteins, and hei2015_refined_grains; grams/day in hei2015_polyunsaturated_fat, hei2015_monounsaturated_fat, and hei2015_saturated_fat; mg/day in hei2015_sodium; and teaspoon equivalents/day in hei2015_added_sugars. Canonical mapping fields omit the hei2015_ prefix. Food-group totals must already include legumes in both vegetable and protein components as specified by HEI-2015. Total fruits include juice; whole fruits do not.

  • diet_value: A direct percentile for "dash", "hei2015", or the backward-compatible generic "percentile" method. Supply a DASH or HEI-2015 percentile from 0 to 100, calculated against the relevant reference distribution. The function does not rank supplied rows against one another. If this column is absent or missing, the diet score is missing. MEPA and raw-intake calls require it to be absent or entirely missing.

  • moderate_activity_minutes and vigorous_activity_minutes: Weekly minutes. Each vigorous minute counts as two moderate-equivalent minutes.

  • smoking_status: One of "never", "former", or "current".

  • years_since_quit: Years since quitting combustible tobacco. This is used only when smoking_status is "former".

  • current_inhaled_nds: Whether an inhaled nicotine-delivery system is currently used.

  • secondhand_smoke_home: Whether the adult lives with an active indoor smoker.

  • sleep_hours: Average hours of sleep per night.

  • bmi: Body mass index in kg/m^2. Values below 18.5 are not scored because the AHA advisory defers to clinician judgment for underweight adults.

  • bmi_profile: Either "general" or "asian_pacific". The function never infers a profile from race or ethnicity.

  • non_hdl_cholesterol: Non-HDL cholesterol in mg/dL.

  • lipid_lowering_treatment: Whether the lipid value is drug treated.

  • diabetes: Whether diabetes has been diagnosed.

  • glucose_measure: Either "fasting_glucose" or "hba1c".

  • glucose_value: Fasting glucose in mg/dL or HbA1c in percent, as named by glucose_measure. Diagnosed diabetes requires HbA1c. A record with no diabetes diagnosis but a value in the diagnostic diabetes range is rejected because the AHA scoring table does not assign that combination.

  • systolic_bp and diastolic_bp: Blood pressure in mm Hg.

  • antihypertensive_treatment: Whether the blood pressure is treated.

Component input columns may contain missing values or be omitted. A component score is NA_real_ when its available inputs are insufficient. Missing values are never imputed. A warning is emitted when an entire LE8 component cannot be calculated for any observation.

Optional clinical-judgment columns

  • apply_lean_muscular_bmi_override: A caller-adjudicated flag asserting that a lean, higher-muscle-mass adult in the general BMI profile has a BMI from 25 to less than 30 and should receive 100 BMI points. If absent, the standard BMI band is used.

  • apply_sleep_apnea_penalty: If TRUE, subtract 20 points for untreated or undertreated sleep apnea. If absent, no discretionary penalty is applied.

  • apply_prediabetes_metformin_penalty: A caller-adjudicated flag asserting that the adult has a history of prediabetes, is taking metformin to prevent diabetes, is currently normoglycemic, and the clinician chose to apply the AHA's discretionary 20-point decrement. If absent, no discretionary penalty is applied.

Source-constrained behavior

The function derives the 0-to-16 MEPA total from the 16 raw screener responses. Raw DASH scoring uses the eight-component Fung index: five food groups receive 1 to 5 points by intake quintile; sodium, red/processed meat, and sweetened beverages receive 5 to 1. Intakes equal to a quintile cutpoint stay in the lower quintile. Their sum is dash_total (8 to 40).

Raw HEI-2015 calls compute 13 density, fatty-acid-ratio, and energy-percentage components with proportional scoring between the published standards. Added sugars use 16 kcal per teaspoon equivalent; saturated fat uses 9 kcal per gram. Scores are capped at each component's maximum. Their sum is hei2015_total (0 to 100), which is distinct from the LE8 diet score. With zero saturated fat and positive unsaturated fat, the fatty-acid component receives 10 points; with all three fats zero it receives zero, following the NCI scoring macro. Missing inputs are never treated as zero; a total requires all of its diet components, regardless of min_components.

Raw DASH and HEI-2015 totals are converted to LE8 scores of 0, 25, 50, 80, or 100 using fixed reference total-score cutpoints. Equality enters the higher LE8 band. Explicit cutpoints override the packaged reference and must come from a suitable fixed reference population, using appropriate survey weights and strata where applicable. Cutpoints are never inferred from data. For references requiring different cutpoints by stratum, score strata in separate calls. Alternatively, diet_method = "percentile" accepts externally calculated DASH or HEI-2015 percentiles. The rows in data are never ranked against one another.

The AHA table applies 20-point treatment decrements to blood-lipid and blood-pressure scores. These components are floored at zero, consistent with the AHA's 0-to-100 metric definition. Optional sleep-apnea and prediabetes/metformin decrements are applied only through explicit flags. Inputs are not rounded. The documented MEPA daily/weekly equivalences are applied where the source question and criterion use different timeframes. Combinations without a source-defined score, including simultaneous current combustible smoking and current inhaled-NDS use, produce a structured error.

References

Lloyd-Jones DM, Allen NB, Anderson CAM, et al. (2022). Life's Essential 8: Updating and Enhancing the American Heart Association's Construct of Cardiovascular Health. Circulation, 146(5), e18-e43. doi:10.1161/CIR.0000000000001078

Lloyd-Jones DM, Ning H, Labarthe D, et al. (2022). Status of Cardiovascular Health in US Adults and Children Using the American Heart Association's New Life's Essential 8 Metrics. Circulation, 146(11), 822-835. doi:10.1161/CIRCULATIONAHA.122.060911

Fung TT, Chiuve SE, McCullough ML, et al. (2008). Adherence to a DASH-Style Diet and Risk of Coronary Heart Disease and Stroke in Women. Archives of Internal Medicine, 168(7), 713-720. doi:10.1001/archinte.168.7.713

Krebs-Smith SM, Pannucci TE, Subar AF, et al. (2018). Update of the Healthy Eating Index: HEI-2015. Journal of the Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics, 118(9), 1591-1602. doi:10.1016/j.jand.2018.05.021 See also the National Cancer Institute's scoring standards and algorithm.

Examples

library(dplyr)
#> 
#> Attaching package: ‘dplyr’
#> The following objects are masked from ‘package:stats’:
#> 
#>     filter, lag
#> The following objects are masked from ‘package:base’:
#> 
#>     intersect, setdiff, setequal, union

patient <- tibble(
  id = "patient_1",
  age = 55,
  sex = "female",
  # Daily servings
  olive_oil = 2,
  green_leafy_vegetables = 1,
  other_vegetables = 2,
  whole_grains = 2,
  # Weekly servings
  berries = 3,
  other_fruit = 5,
  meat = 2,
  fish = 3,
  chicken = 2,
  cheese = 1,
  butter_cream = 1,
  beans = 3,
  sweets_and_pastries = 1,
  nuts = 4,
  alcohol = 4,
  # Fast-food meals per week
  fast_food = 0,
  moderate_activity_minutes = 90,
  vigorous_activity_minutes = 0,
  smoking_status = "former",
  years_since_quit = 6,
  current_inhaled_nds = FALSE,
  secondhand_smoke_home = FALSE,
  sleep_hours = 7.5,
  bmi = 27.5,
  bmi_profile = "general",
  non_hdl_cholesterol = 145,
  lipid_lowering_treatment = FALSE,
  diabetes = FALSE,
  glucose_measure = "fasting_glucose",
  glucose_value = 95,
  systolic_bp = 128,
  diastolic_bp = 78,
  antihypertensive_treatment = FALSE
)

scores <- score_le8(patient, diet_method = "mepa")
select(scores, id, mepa_total, le8_diet_score, le8_composite_score,
       le8_category)
#>          id mepa_total le8_diet_score le8_composite_score le8_category
#> 1 patient_1         14             80                  80         high
